newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila to use Westinghouse gas turbines.
newsitem.headline: Manila to use Westinghouse gas turbines.

text.p: State-owned National Power Corp (Napocor) said on Monday it planned to use its two 501 gas turbines for a 244-megawatt power plant in the southern island of Mindanao.

The gas turbines, worth $30 million each, were part of the settlement between Westinghouse Electric Corp and the Philippine government in 1995 over a dispute involving the construction of a 620-mw nuclear power plant located north of the capital that was never commissioned.

Napocor chairman Francisco Viray told reporters the turbines may be used for the 244-mw combined cycle power plant based on a revised programme still to be approved by the board. The plant would be operational by the year 2000.
Earlier, a Napocor official said Marubeni Corp had offered to buy the two 501F units for its power project in Colombia.
